Work along in your IDE, on `index.qmd`, the report of the housing-audit workspace
:::

::: notes
The last session of the day takes apart the document on which the whole course leans, the report of the workspace. It is a Quarto document: a file that holds prose and code together and becomes a finished report when it is rendered, running its code on the way. Every workspace of the course has one, whatever its case, and the one on my screen is the report of the housing-audit case. We take it in four steps. First, what such a file holds and what rendering does to it. Then the header and the chunks of code, with the options that change what a chunk shows. Then the places where numbers, figures and references enter the text. And last a render from a clean session, which is the test that a report makes everything that it uses.
:::

# Source and output {#source-and-output .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Section 1
:::

::: notes
Section one is about the difference between a source and its output. A Quarto document is plain text, and we start with why that matters. Then the three kinds of content that the file holds, and the two programs that turn it into a report when you render it. Then we open the report of the workspace in Positron, run its chunks one at a time in the console, and preview the whole report, which is the first task of your own.
:::
